Maharashtra heatwave: Dahanu sizzles at 38.5 degrees Celsius, Mumbai records 37.5 degrees Celsius as temperatures soar above normal
Dahanu recorded the highest maximum temperature in the Konkan-Goa region at 38.5 degrees Celsius, 4.8 degrees above normal. Mumbai followed with 37.5 degrees Celsius, four degrees above normal, while Ratnagiri recorded 37.3 degrees Celsius, 4.4 degrees above normal

Dahanu recorded the highest maximum temperature in the Konkan-Goa region at 38.5 degrees Celsius, 4.8 degrees above normal. File Pic
Daytime temperatures remained significantly above normal across Maharashtra on Thursday, according to Maharashtra's weather bulletin, with Dahanu recording the state's highest maximum temperature at 38.5 degrees Celsius, 4.8 degrees above normal. Mumbai recorded 37.5 degrees Celsius, four degrees above normal, as hot and dry conditions prevailed across most regions.
Mahabaleshwar recorded the state's lowest minimum temperature at 18 degrees Celsius, while several stations reported warmer-than-normal nights.

Smith will work with UB co-investigators Riana Pryor, Ph.D., associate professor of exercise and nutritional sciences, and Jihnhee Yu, Ph.D., professor of biostatistics, both in the School of Public Health and Health Professions. Sarah Febres Cordero, Ph.D., an assistant professor of nursing at Emory University, is also part of the research team.
“Restaurant workers are surrounded by heat every day, yet they have largely been left out of the occupational heat conversation,” Smith said.
Smith, who also serves as a nurse scientist for La Isla Network, has conducted extensive research on the effects of climate change on the health of marginalized populations. La Isla Network brings together universities, researchers, government institutions and companies to address heat stress and other climate-related risks.
Occupational heat exposure is often associated with outdoor jobs, such as agriculture and construction. However, millions of restaurant workers face prolonged exposure to high temperatures while working near ovens, stoves and fryers.
“While heat exposure has been studied extensively in outdoor occupations, we know surprisingly little about its impact on the health of indoor service workers, particularly their kidney health,” Smith said.
The research team will assess workplace conditions and workers’ health during actual shifts. Researchers will measure environmental temperatures, body temperature, hydration levels, heat-related symptoms and changes in kidney function.

XRP Is 63% Below Its All-Time High and Ethereum 51%. Which Reclaims their ATH First?
XRP and Ethereum both sit far below their 2025 peaks, and the path back looks very different for each coin. ETF flows, banking partnerships, and upcoming upgrades will determine which one gets there first.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) trades at $1.33, 63.5% below its all-time high of $3.65 set on July 17, 2025. In comparison, Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) is priced at $2,403, roughly 51.4% below its peak of $4,946 reached on August 24, 2025.
Both cryptocurrencies have fallen over the last month, with XRP down 13.8% and Ethereum down 12.6%. In the past 24 hours, XRP has fluctuated between $1.32 and $1.40, while Ethereum has traded between $2,396 and $2,519.
The drive to reclaim their all-time highs motivates many investors. Those who bought during the 2025 surge would still be in profit today. To reach their former highs, XRP needs a 174.4% increase, while Ethereum needs a 105.9% gain. So, in the battle of XRP vs. Ethereum, which coin is more likely to hit its all-time high first?
What XRP and Ethereum Would Be Worth Back at Their Records
Market capitalization, calculated by multiplying a coin’s current price by its circulating supply, is a crucial factor in evaluating potential price targets. Currently, XRP has a market cap of about $83.85 billion, with 63.13 billion tokens in circulation. By comparison, Ethereum has a market cap of $293.48 billion and 122.15 million ETH in circulation.
XRP’s supply dynamics pose a challenge. With a maximum supply of 100 billion tokens, a significant portion of XRP has yet to enter circulation. The current fully diluted valuation—what XRP would be worth if all tokens were circulating—stands at $132.81 billion.
This implies that new tokens entering circulation will require additional investment for XRP to reach its previous highs. Additionally, as XRP ranks fifth by market cap, reclaiming its record would mean surpassing larger cryptocurrencies currently above it.
XRP Needs ETF Buyers and Bank Customers to Show Up
To regain its lost value, XRP needs more buyers, particularly through exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and banking partnerships. As of October 21, XRP ETFs held $1.57 billion in net assets, with total net inflows since launch reaching $1.80 billion according to SoSoValue.
However, new investment has slowed to a trickle, with the funds taking in just $708,500 on October 21 after two days of no inflows and a $2.47 million outflow on October 16. For reference, these funds had attracted $22.65 million on September 25, during a run of inflows when XRP traded at $1.57 on September 22, but interest waned shortly thereafter.
On a promising note, Germany’s Sparkassen savings banks began offering XRP trading through their banking app on October 19, with plans to integrate around 30 to 40 more banks each month. However, XRP’s daily trading volume showed little change on its launch day.
Additionally, the proposed lending amendment for the XRP Ledger, designed to enable direct borrowing and lending within the network, still needs more validator votes, the independent servers that approve ledger changes. If this amendment gains approval, it could create new demand for XRP.
Ethereum Has Wall Street Rails but Weak ETF Flows
Unlike XRP, Ethereum now has a major bank’s payment token running on its network. JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM | JPM Price Prediction) announced on October 19 the integration of JPM Coin, a deposit token, onto Ethereum’s main public network. A deposit token is a digital version of a bank deposit operating on a blockchain.
However, Ethereum has also faced ETF outflows, with $201.89 million leaving on October 6 and $103.28 million on October 19, according to SoSoValue. Its cumulative net inflows have decreased from $13.96 billion on September 28 to $12.83 billion on October 21. The modest inflow of about $14.96 million on October 21 marked the first positive flow since October 13.
A positive sign for ETH: 43.8 million ETH are currently staked, indicating many holders have locked their coins to help secure the network in exchange for rewards. This staking reduces the available supply for quick trades, which could affect price movements.
As for upcoming developments, Ethereum’s major upgrade, Glamsterdam, is set to enter the Hoodi test network on October 26, giving developers a platform to test changes before they hit the main network. Looking ahead, Ethereum has long-term projections for 2028.
Which Coin Reclaims Its All-Time High First, XRP or Ethereum?
Given the circumstances, Ethereum appears more likely to reach its all-time high before XRP does. With a 105.9% increase needed compared to XRP’s 174.4%, plus JPM Coin and a sizeable ETF asset base, Ethereum has the edge. However, a smaller required gain doesn’t guarantee a faster recovery. XRP rose 25.1% over the past 90 days, while Ethereum gained 33% in the same timeframe.
For Ethereum, reaching its previous high likely hinges on sustained ETF inflows, followed by breaks above $2,753 (its September 22 price) and $2,967 (its price at the start of 2026). For XRP, ETF inflows would likely need to return to their September rate before XRP reclaims $1.57 and then $1.84. If ETH closes below $2,396 or XRP stays below $1.57 with flat ETF flows, a return to either record before 2027 looks unlikely.

BRS leader T. Harish Rao and others examining a withered paddy field at Burugupalli in Siddipet district on Thursday.

The drought conditions in the State were not due to nature’s impact but due to the failures of the Congress Government and the Chief Minister was in a deep slumber even when standing crops in 12 lakh acres were withering, former minister and Deputy Floor Leader of the BRS Legislature Party T. Harish Rao alleged.
Speaking after examining the withered crops, mostly paddy, at Burugupalli of Gajwel mandal in Siddipet district on Thursday, he said the previous BRS Government had provided a helping hand to the farming community during the Covid-19 pandemic and achieve one-crore tonnes of paddy production, the Revanth Reddy Government had announced crop holiday in the name of El Nino impact.
Despite the forecast and warnings given by Met scientists on the El Nino impact 10 months in advance, the State Government had failed to maintain sufficient coal stocks at the thermal power stations and also failed to procure energy in advance. Now, the Chief Minister was washing his hands by stating that there was no energy in the market for procurement, though the government was ready to purchase it at any cost.
Mr. Harish Rao faulted the government for its failure to switch on/run the motors 24x7 at Kannepally, Devadula and Kalwakurthy lifts to ensure sufficient water for irrigation and drinking needs.
He mentioned that neighbouring Maharashtra Government had released ₹5,000 per acre immediate relief to farmers and Andhra Pradesh had declared drought mandals. But, the Telangana Government had not even declared drought mandals.
Criticising the government for burdening people with ₹5,420 crore of energy charges in the form of true-up charges, the BRS leader demanded that the government announce drought mandals immediately and extend ₹12,000 per farm worker, as promised in the Congress election manifesto.

New Delhi, Oct. 22 -- On 21 October, widespread disclosures brought to light a little-known Indian company, eMudhra Ltd. At its heart were digital 'certificates', which the company allegedly left unprotected on the internet-thereby making its users highly susceptible to fraud. Compounding this is the fact that eMudhra is the only Indian issuer of digital certificates trusted by websites worldwide. Mint explains the debacle and what it might mean for the internet in India.
Founded in 2008 by Venkatraman Srinivasan, eMudhra Ltd is a Bengaluru-based company that offers digital identity verification, cybersecurity, paperless work management, and associated services. The company went public on 1 June 2022 in a Rs.412.79 crore initial public offering, with 60% of the proceeds from the promoters' sale of shares. In FY26, it reported Rs.701.6 crore in operating revenue and Rs.110 crore in net profit.
Srinivasan, the founder and executive chairman, holds 17.3% of the company. Other promoters alongside Srinivasan collectively hold 54.4% of the company. Globally, the company has six international subsidiaries in Mauritius, UAE, US, Singapore, the Netherlands and Indonesia. Some popular services that eMudhra offers include digital signatures for India's income tax and provident fund forms, trusted identity and multi-step verification within companies, and paperless document verification.
The other side of eMudhra's business, which certifies whether a website is secure, is the one that was seemingly compromised here.
On 17 October, an independent cybersecurity researcher disclosed on Mozilla's public, open-source web browser cybersecurity incident tracker that websites using eMudhra's digital certificates could be compromised.
Put very simply, eMudhra is one of a handful of companies registered on the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)'s Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA) list. Interestingly, it is currently the only company from India that is a recognised digital certificate issuer trusted by most web browsers worldwide, including Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Apple Safari, and Mozilla's own Firefox.
The flaw pertained to eMudhra's digital certificates themselves. One way websites identify themselves as authentic is through digital certificates, which encrypt a website's information using complex cryptographic keys-a string of 115 characters generated by digital randomness. This 'key' is so long and comes in so many permutations and combinations that classical computers could take decades to guess just one.
Instead of such a complicated key, eMudhra's digital certificates appeared to show keys that were extremely simple and would allow almost anyone with a basic laptop to spoof, guess and then breach. For instance, when users open a banking website, the site uses a mechanism called Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt the user's data with a certifying authority's digital keys, preventing cyber attackers from stealing it.
Such an incident, the original cybersecurity report said, revealed a lack of emphasis on security at eMudhra for tasks that could be highly critical and sensitive.
In a statement issued on BSE on 21 October, eMudhra claimed that the weak security keys were generated due to a technical 'flaw' and that the company is 'working to establish the root cause'.
On this note, eMudhra further claimed that it had not experienced any cyber breach and remained in full control of its security infrastructure. It also claimed that the global digital certificate business was different from its Indian digital signature business, for which it remains in MeitY's trusted certifiers list. "The global TLS business runs on infrastructure that is completely separate from the India DSC (digital signature certificate) business. DSC and eSign services in India are running normally," it further added.
For its global clients, eMudhra said it is working to prevent disruptions to critical services worldwide and to fix the certification process.
Globally, users may see alerts about data breaches or the suspension of banking services in isolated cases, though no such cases have been reported yet. MeitY, on this note, issued a statement taking note of the incident, issuing a statement on Wednesday evening that said, "MeitY has taken serious note of the reported incident. A special team has been constituted to investigate the matter." The nodal ministry, however, claimed that the entire impact falls on eMudhra's global business division, which MeitY is not responsible for auditing.
Independently, eMudhra claimed in its statement on Wednesday morning that it has cleared security audits conducted by all the above-cited web browsers, as required.
eMudhra also claimed that the impact on its revenue would be 1%-around Rs.7 crore ($750,000), per FY26 earnings. However, it further added that the incident "may have some reputational risks on eMudhra which cannot be quantified."
Since the incident was disclosed, eMudhra's shares have fallen by 37% as of press time. After hitting a lower circuit on BSE on Wednesday, eMudhra was trading 18.8% lower until press time on Thursday.
It is difficult to ascertain if the weak security keys by eMudhra have directly led to any breach. Interestingly, on the same day that eMudhra acknowledged its weak certification keys, India's largest banker, State Bank of India, published a statement stating that 3,897 of its users had their personally identifiable information disclosed online.
"The exposed information reportedly included customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files," the SBI statement read.
While the two incidents could not be materially linked, breaches that could lead to SBI's data being leaked online may occur more frequently if weak encryption keys are used to verify a website-creating scope for attackers to steal sensitive information without being detected.
For now, there have been no clearly disclosed, direct breaches resulting from the incident.Disclaimer Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from MINT.
